title: The permission heist
summary: Friday's deploy died with "Permission denied" and Gary's answer was chmod 777. Do it properly: read rwx, lock down a secret, fix owners and groups, and write a tight sudo rule.

nodes.jammie: the app server; user deploy runs the deploys

tasks.title: Case the joint
tasks.text: Read the crime scene first: `cat /srv/app/deploy.log`. Then look at the secret file `/etc/app/secret.conf`. What are its permissions right now, as a **3-digit octal number** (like `750`)?
hints: `ls -l /etc/app/secret.conf` shows something like `-rw-r--r--`. Skip the first character (the file type), then read three groups of three: **owner**, **group**, **others**.
Score each group: r = 4, w = 2, x = 1, and add up. `rw-` = 6, `r--` = 4, `---` = 0. So `-rw-r--r--` is 644.
Or let Linux do the maths: `stat -c %a /etc/app/secret.conf`.

tasks.title: Lock up the secret
tasks.text: A database password that **everyone** on the server can read is a heist waiting to happen. Make `/etc/app/secret.conf` owned by user `root` and group `deployers`, readable by its group, and not accessible at all to others. Only root may change it.

checks.fail_msg: The owner should be root and the group deployers.
The permissions should be 640: owner read+write, group read, others nothing.

hints: `chown user:group file` changes both owner and group (`chgrp group file` changes only the group).
`chmod 640 file`: 6 (rw-) for the owner, 4 (r--) for the group, 0 (---) for everyone else. In letters: `chmod u=rw,g=r,o= file`.

tasks.title: Join the crew
tasks.text: The secret is now readable by group `deployers`, but user `deploy` isn't in that group. Add them, **without** removing them from any other group.

checks.fail_msg: deploy is not in the deployers group yet (check with: id deploy).
deploy lost its own group: use usermod -aG (the a means append).

hints: `usermod -aG deployers deploy`. The **a** (append) matters: `-G` alone replaces all of the user's extra groups. (`gpasswd -a deploy deployers` does the same.)
Group changes apply to **new** logins. A shell that was already open as deploy keeps its old groups.

tasks.title: Make the script runnable
tasks.text: `/srv/app/deploy.sh` can't be run at all: nobody has the **x** (execute) permission. Fix it so that `deploy` can **run** it but not **change** it, and users outside the deployers group can't read or run it. (Hint: Gary's `chmod 777` fails two of those three rules.)

checks.fail_msg: deploy can modify deploy.sh. Only root should be able to change it.
Others (users outside the file's group) can still read or run deploy.sh.

hints: Same idea as the secret: give the file to group `deployers`, and give that group read + execute.
`chgrp deployers /srv/app/deploy.sh && chmod 750 /srv/app/deploy.sh`: owner (root) rwx, group r-x, others nothing. A script needs **r** as well as **x**, because the shell has to read it to run it.

tasks.title: The deploy goes through
tasks.text: Try it as the deploy user: `su - deploy -c /srv/app/deploy.sh`. One more "Permission denied" stands in the way. Fix it (properly!) so the deploy succeeds.

checks.fail_msg: Running /srv/app/deploy.sh as deploy still fails. Run it yourself to see the error.
Works, but now everybody can write to /srv/app/releases. Give write access to deploy (or its group) only.

hints: The script writes into `/srv/app/releases`. `ls -ld /srv/app/releases` (the `-d` shows the folder itself, not its contents): who owns it?

Writing a **new file** in a folder needs **w** on the folder. Either give the folder to deploy (`chown deploy:deployers /srv/app/releases`) or to the group with group write (`chgrp deployers ... && chmod 775 ...`).

tasks.title: One key, one door
tasks.text: After a deploy, `deploy` must restart the oven with `sudo /usr/local/bin/restart-oven`, **without** a password prompt (it runs unattended). It must **not** be able to run anything else as root. Write that sudo rule.

checks.fail_msg: The sudo configuration has a syntax error. Run visudo -c to see it.
deploy cannot run sudo /usr/local/bin/restart-oven without a password yet.
deploy can run other commands as root too. Allow only restart-oven.

hints: Rules go in a file under `/etc/sudoers.d/`. A rule reads: **who** `host=(as whom)` **options: command**.
`deploy ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/bin/restart-oven`. Give the full path to the command: a bare name could match anything.
Write it with `visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/deploy`, or with echo, then `chmod 440` the file and check it with `visudo -c`. A broken sudoers file can lock everyone out of sudo.
